messages:
harper: dropped a prototype for a 'Workload mode' toggle that switches autoscale behavior between 'interactive' and 'batch' workloads. figma: https://figma.com/file/workload-mode

leila: interesting. main UX question: does mode change global (org) or per-route? design currently shows per-deployment which matches product ask, but we should clarify in microcopy.

noah: per-deployment makes sense. implementation note: interactive mode keeps lower latency targets and smaller burst, batch mode favors throughput and larger burst windows.

josh: copy concern: the toggle label 'Interactive / Batch' might be unclear to new users. propose tooltips: 'Interactive — low latency, small scale bursts' and 'Batch — high throughput, relaxed latency'.

a11y-bot: lint: toggle lacks accessible label; tooltip content not accessible via keyboard; color contrast on the mode chips fails on small text.

harper: good catches. other design ideas: when user flips to Batch mode, disable SLO slider or change its unit explanation to 'Target average latency' since p95 doesn't make sense for bulk jobs.

leila: prefer not to disable controls entirely. instead change labels/context: SLO slider becomes 'Latency objective (informational in Batch mode)' and show a badge 'Best-effort' to avoid confusion.

noah: runtime behavior: switching mode toggles autoscale algorithm parameter sets: e.g., aggressive_scale_down=false for interactive, backfill_window=300s for batch. UX should surface that these are algorithm presets.

josh: could we show a small expandable 'What changes' panel listing the key algorithm diffs? that would help power users.

a11y-bot: reminder: dynamic panel must be focus-trapped when expanded and have aria-describedby linking to the toggle so screen reader users understand the relation.

harper: also adding a 'Preview impact' snapshot when switching mode would be useful: show expected median latency, p95 (if available), estimated cost change, and suggested min/max changes.

leila: snapshot design: prefer showing absolute numbers and a short text rationale. e.g. 'Expected median latency: 120ms 370ms during warm-up' (maybe too much?).

noah: runtime can provide median and tail estimates for both modes. note: for Batch mode we only have median and throughput estimates, not p95. UX should reflect that gracefully.

josh: microcopy: when p95 is unavailable show 'p95 not estimated for Batch mode' with link 'why' that explains metric relevance. avoid alarmist phrasing.

a11y-bot: SR suggestion: when metric unavailable present a spoken explanation: 'P ninety-five latency is not estimated in Batch mode because scheduling dynamics differ.'

harper: guardrail idea: prevent users from enabling a very low SLO in Batch mode by greying the slider below a recommended minimum and show tooltip 'Not recommended for batch processing'.

leila: alternatively, allow setting but show a persistent inline warning: 'Setting low p95 in Batch mode may cause unnecessary cost without benefit.' This respects user control while informing them.

noah: instrumentation: include which preset was applied in telemetry: workload_mode:batch|interactive, preset_id, forecast_snapshot. useful for later tuning.

josh: keyboard flow: if preview snapshot appears after toggle, focus should go to the snapshot's heading and SR announce short summary. current prototype leaves focus on the toggle which is confusing.

a11y-bot: auto-lint: ensure names for the two mode options, add aria-pressed states for the toggle, and provide offscreen SR-only text for the preview numbers spelled out (e.g., 'estimated cost increase: twenty percent').

harper: UX copy iteration for the mode chip tooltip: 'Interactive — prioritizes low latency for requests; autoscaler favors smaller, faster adjustments.' vs 'Batch — prioritizes throughput and cost efficiency; autoscaler favors larger scale steps and longer ramps.'

leila: small visual: show a subtle sparkline in the preview reflecting expected request pattern: spiky for interactive, sustained for batch. chart needs alt text.

noah: backend note: when users switch from Batch to Interactive, we should surface the warmup time for caches & KV (e.g., 'Expected warmup: 2020s') so they understand temporary latency.

josh: final ask: add an account-level default for workload mode and allow users to 'Apply to all routes' with clear confirmation; include a transient banner when applied at org-level.

a11y-bot: checklist before merge: toggle keyboard operable, aria labels for tooltips, preview SR text, color contrast checks, focus management, and explicit language for numbers.

harper: thanks all. i'll update Figma with the wording, add the preview snapshot, and include SR-only strings. will post updated frame as 2149876558. tagging @design-review for a quick pass :eyes:
